name: Finero Public API
description:
Tenant-scoped public API for Finero — AR / cash-flow automation. Authenticate every request with `Authorization: Bearer <API key>` (keys are created in Settings → API and are tenant-owned). All data belongs to the key's tenant; no request input can address another tenant. Two permissions exist: **admin** keys can call every operation; **readonly** keys only operations without side effects (`x-permission: readonly`). Lists are cursor-paginated (limit 1–100, follow pagination.next_cursor). Request bodies are capped at 64 KiB. Rate limits: 120/min per key and 600/min per tenant, both fixed 60-second windows. EVERY response that reached the limiter carries `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining`, `RateLimit-Reset` (seconds until the window resets) and `RateLimit-Policy` (both quotas, static), plus the same figures as the newer combined `RateLimit` field. Pace against them rather than waiting to be refused. The triple describes whichever quota is CLOSEST TO REFUSING, so a key that is fine may still show little headroom when the tenant is busy. The counters are shared server-side, not per-instance, so the numbers are exact rather than approximate. Requests rejected BEFORE the limiter — unknown path, bad credentials, wrong method — consume no quota and carry no rate-limit fields. 429 adds `Retry-After` in seconds (RFC 9110); waiting that long is enough, and retrying sooner is refused again. Failed-authentication attempts are limited separately per source IP; that quota is deliberately not published. The windows are FIXED rather than sliding, so a burst spanning a boundary can pass up to twice the limit before being refused — do not treat the limit as a hard ceiling over less than two windows. `RateLimit-Remaining` RISES when a window rolls, for the same reason; an increase is the quota refilling, not an error. Watch `RateLimit-Reset` jump upward to tell a roll from a miscount. A 503 is not the limiter: under extreme concurrency the platform sheds load before the request reaches Finero, so it carries neither rate-limit fields nor Retry-After. Back off and retry. Decimal money amounts are exact strings (never floats); *_minor amounts are integers in the currency's minor unit. Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC.

**There is a second way in.** This API is for systems and unattended automation, authenticated by a tenant API key that acts as the WORKSPACE. If instead a person is present and connecting an AI assistant to their own workspace, use the Finero MCP server at `https://app.getfinero.com/mcp` — Model Context Protocol over the Streamable HTTP transport (JSON-RPC 2.0, `MCP-Protocol-Version` 2026-07-28, 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26), authorized with OAuth 2.1 so the session acts as THAT PERSON. Its `server.json` manifest — the MCP registry's published format — is at `https://app.getfinero.com/mcp/server.json`. It is read-mostly — 24 tools (list_tasks, dismiss_task, summarize_aging, list_customer_aging, list_aging_installments, list_invoices, summarize_invoices, get_invoice, list_payment_integrations, list_payments, list_workflows, list_workflow_executions, list_erp_connections, list_sync_runs, get_sync_run, start_erp_sync, list_payment_links, get_payment_link, create_payment_links, list_scheduled_emails, update_scheduled_email, delete_scheduled_email, push_payment_receipts, deactivate_payment_link). An agent may do what its person may: issue payment links (one, or a split of up to 12) and withdraw them, and reschedule or cancel their emails; an admin's agent may also start an ERP sync and release held receipts to the ERP. It can never send email it has written, or take or move money. Its OAuth scopes are declared in RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata at `https://app.getfinero.com/mcp/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`, which also names the authorization server. The two are not interchangeable: if you hold an API key, use this API.
